solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second pun — could one be foiled by it?

definitions.text: could one be foiled by it?

parts.note: a pun is a piece of verbal play on words

explanation.surface: A writer offers a quip and wonders whether a rival could parry it.
explanation.walkthrough: A foil is a light fencing sword, so 'foiled' hints at fencing rather than being thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing with foils is the classic form of sword fighting, so a fencer could be beaten in it.

clue.text: Close company

parts.note: to shut down a business formally is to liquidate it, a phrase meaning bring to an end

explanation.surface: A tightly knit group of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close company' reads as intimate friends; it is really the instruction to close down a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquidating a business is described as winding it up, the formal closing of a company.

clue.text: Discount variable base rate, not so

indicators.note: variable means the letters of the following words can change their order

parts.note: the words base rate supply the letter pool, taken as written
so and as both mean in that way, as in 'so/as good as'

explanation.surface: A bank customer asks for a discount on a fluctuating base rate.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'not so' removes AS from BASE RATE, and 'variable' rearranges the remaining BERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is money returned or deducted from a price, which is a kind of discount.

clue.text: In preference it's not included at church

indicators.note: not included means these letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: giving priority to something means preferring it
the word it, from the contracted it's

explanation.surface: Someone explains what is left out of a church's order of preferences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not included' removes IT from PRIORITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a religious house whose church is run by a prior, so it can stand for a church.

clue.text: One needs to set one's sights high when using it

definitions.text: One needs to set one's sights high when using it

parts.words: One needs to set one's sights high when using it
parts.note: setting one's sights high usually means being ambitious, but here the gun sights are aimed at the sky to hit planes

explanation.surface: Advice about ambition: aim high when you take something on.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for ambition is taken literally: the weapon's sights point upward at aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon designed to shoot down planes must be aimed upward into the sky.

clue.text: Bait male? Wrong, wrong!

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters are put the wrong way, rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler discovers a mistake about the sex of the fish bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges MALE and WRONG together.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms used by anglers as fishing bait are called this, after the angling they serve.

clue.text: Moulding style of presentation I have followed

parts.note: a format is the way something is laid out or presented
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A designer describes a moulding style used for a presentation they followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moulding' reads as a noun for decorative trim; it is the adjective meaning shaping.
explanation.definitionFit: Formative means shaping or developing, so a formative influence is moulding someone.

clue.text: Turn over map to find pad

parts.note: to flip something is to turn it over
a chart is a map, especially a nautical one

explanation.surface: A navigator turns over the map to find something to write on.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pad of paper sheets on a stand, flipped over during presentations, is this item.

clue.text: Posh Colin's turn to get straight

parts.note: U means upper-class, a British usage for posh

indicators.note: a turn here is a twist that reorders the letters of the name

parts.note: the name Colin, its 's a link to turn

explanation.surface: A posh man called Colin gets his chance to put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a long-standing British label for posh usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind a coil is to straighten it out, the opposite of winding up.

clue.text: Intoxication from tiny beer I ordered!

indicators.note: ordered suggests putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their drunkenness came from a very small beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges TINY BEER I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriety is a formal word for drunkenness, the state of being intoxicated.

clue.text: Refuse to talk about said meat at university

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: said shows the word that follows is heard, not seen

parts.note: lamb is a meat
being up means in residence at university, a British usage

explanation.surface: A diner declines to discuss what they were told about the meat at college.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMB, when said, gives LAM: the B is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To go silent and decline to say anything is the idiom for shutting up like a shellfish.

clue.text: Relentless assassin

definitions.meaning: a killer who slits victims' throats

explanation.surface: A description of a merciless hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fiercely competitive and a murderer, from slitting throats.

clue.text: Exchange one to be replaced by a sample

indicators.note: replaced by tells us one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: to switch is to exchange
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone swaps one item for a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced by' swaps the I in SWITCH for A.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch is a small piece of cloth used as a sample of fabric.

clue.text: Bet about magistrate taking on belligerent person

indicators.note: about means the bet surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a wager is a bet

indicators.note: taking means the magistrate takes on the next piece, joining it

parts.note: RM stands for Resident Magistrate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on a magistrate taking on an aggressive defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: RM, Resident Magistrate, was a title once used in Ireland and British colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A warmonger is someone who stirs up or advocates war, a hostile aggressor.

clue.text: They are compulsory for the players

definitions.text: They are compulsory for the players

parts.words: They are compulsory for the players
parts.note: in music, obligatory instrumental parts that must be played and not omitted

explanation.surface: Rules that sportsmen must obey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests sport; it means musicians, and the Italian musical term means obligatory.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, obbligato parts are accompaniments marked essential that performers must not leave out.

clue.text: Gloomy reply about first person in Rouen's clothing

indicators.note: about shows the reply is placed around, here after, the first person

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling gloomy
je is French for I, the first person, Rouen being a French city
ANS is the short form of answer, a reply

explanation.surface: A gloomy answer about a Frenchman's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rouen points to French, where 'I' is JE.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim trousers dyed indigo are a common item of casual clothing.

clue.text: Old craft floating home

definitions.meaning: Noah's vessel housed his family and animals afloat

explanation.surface: An old boat now used as a houseboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's vessel was an ancient craft that served as a floating home for all aboard.

clue.text: Bandit held moreover

indicators.note: held means the word sits inside, contained by the bandit's letters

explanation.surface: A criminal was arrested, and what's more there is more to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words add a further point, as in 'and another thing'.

clue.text: Opener of vital performance

definitions.meaning: crucial, as in a ... player or ... performance

explanation.surface: The opening act of an important show.
explanation.definitionFit: A key opens locks, and as an adjective key means crucial or of great importance.

clue.text: Where one may go could be determined by accident

definitions.text: Where one may go could be determined by accident

parts.words: Where one may go could be determined by accident
parts.note: a destination decided by chance, but literally a driver whose route is set by where a crash happened

explanation.surface: A musing on chance shaping one's travels in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by accident' reads as by chance; it is a road accident that sends the emergency driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramedic crews drive to the scene of crashes, so their destination is set by the accident.

clue.text: Not drinking this wine perhaps

definitions.meaning: a wine that is not sweet, such as a sec

explanation.surface: A teetotaller declines a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means teetotal, free of alcohol, and also describes a wine that is not sweet.

clue.text: After end of term, one place setting

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of term

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
lieu is French for place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: After the term ends, someone lays a single place setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is linking here; the parse is M, I, LIEU in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a social environment or surroundings, the setting one lives in.

clue.text: Robe on round lady first

indicators.note: first means the lady's name comes at the front

parts.note: Kim is a woman's name
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dress is put on a rounded woman before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts KIM ahead of ON and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a long, loose Japanese robe with wide sleeves.

clue.text: Motor home

parts.note: a camper van to live in, but here read as a building that houses a car

explanation.surface: A camper van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motor home' suggests a camper van; read it as the home of a motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: A building attached to a house where a car is kept is effectively the vehicle's home.

clue.text: Crowd round

definitions.meaning: a group of people, as in one's social set

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a group of associates and also a ring-shaped figure.

clue.text: Statement's invalid if David's fat son and daughter abscond

definitions.note: statement is, the 's linking it to the rest

indicators.note: invalid suggests the letters are not valid as written and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the S of David's included, as the letter pool

explanation.surface: A sworn document is void because a fat man's children ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'abscond' takes S and D from IF DAVIDS FAT; 'invalid' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a written statement confirmed by oath for use as evidence.

clue.text: Mare maybe followed by a third horse, dead worried

indicators.note: followed by means the next pieces come after

parts.note: a nag is an old horse, a mare for example

indicators.note: a third means only the opening third of the word survives, its other letters dropped

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A horse-race report: a mare, then a third horse, a dead heat, worries everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third' keeps only GE, the first third of the six-letter GEEGEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag someone is to worry or pester them persistently.

clue.text: One caring about lack of education

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A teacher worries about pupils' lack of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ONE CARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is lack of knowledge, the result of being uneducated.

clue.text: Offer formerly a few old pence

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
ten is a small number, a few
D was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: An offer once stood at a few pennies in the old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pennies were written d.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend a welcome or an invitation is to offer it.

clue.text: Thwarted by awful crookedness not going to extremes

indicators.note: awful signals the letters are mangled into a new order
not going to extremes means the outermost letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Someone's plans were frustrated by terrible dishonesty that stopped short of excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not going to extremes' drops C and S from CROOKEDNESS; 'awful' rearranges ROOKEDNES.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a player blocked from hitting the ball is stymied, hence the word for being thwarted generally.
